scope: Same natively verified development KZG proof and equal deferred pairing outputs. Native key/shape and claim structure are compiler constants, with claim payloads public; Aiur authenticates key and claims digests as public inputs. Native lowering uses the production two-trace layout and lookup tuning with quotient budget 2. No proof-generation timings or full Init claim.
interpretation: Main advice cells, fixed cells, auxiliary lookup cells, quotient coefficient cells and commitment counts are separate metrics. These are not peak memory or runtime estimates.
The original Aiur verifier already has fewer padded main cells than the handwritten verifier for this identical predecessor proof. It is wider and shallower, with thousands of per-column commitments.
The word16 range change reduces main cells by about 21 percent but removes only 9 main commitments. It does not address the recursive commitment-count problem.
Native keys, proof shape and claim structure are specialized; Aiur parses and authenticates key and claims data. Equal deferred pairing outputs do not make the implementations equally specialized.
No change to capacities, padding rules or verifier acceptance was needed for this diagnostic.
